paragraphs.text: # dsh-butler
English | 中文
`dsh-butler` is the Butler plugin for the DSH App, shipping its browser UI and local host in one pac
kage. The host registers routes, scans extensions, and manages processes through DSH's `webServer` a
nd `subprocess` services. It does not start a standalone Guardian, install a LaunchAgent, or depend
services. It does not start a standalone Guardian, install a LaunchAgent, or depend on Nowledge Mem.
## DSH compatibility
The compatibility declaration is limited to DSH **0.2.0-rc.2 or 0.2.1-rc.2**. Both `engines.dsh` and
the optional peer `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot` use exactly `0.2.0-rc.2 || 0.2.1-rc.2`; the optional
peer describes the host without installing another DSH runtime. It does not claim compatibility with
later prereleases. Recheck Host services, session events, and Client Slots after a DSH upgrade; met
adata and local tests do not replace live App acceptance.
## Working directory
Plugin configuration accepts `workdir`, defaulting to `~/.dsh/butler/`. On first load, the plugin co
pies its built-in generic skeleton; a directory that already contains `butler.json` is not overwritt
en. Personal data, interpreter configuration, and extensions belong to the instance working director
y and can be migrated together. The plugin does not assume a personal workspace.

Relative paths are resolved against the directory containing `butler.json`. Extensions under `tools/
` and `services/` with `hosted.autoStart` resume when the DSH App starts; DSH's subprocess managed r
ange terminates them when the App exits or the plugin unloads. Services do not restart automatically
; tools restart inside the host according to their manifest policy. Bounded commands and reports fro
m `faculties/` also run through the same subprocess integration.
## Host API
Public Host APIs share DSH's same-origin prefix `/myspace-butler/api`; the original client paths `/m
yspace-butler/*` remain compatibility aliases. Routes include `/health`, `/catalog`, `/services`, `/
faculties`, `/runs`, and `/quick-actions`; tool lists come from `/overview`. Both tools and services
support `/:kind/:id/{start,stop,restart}` and `/:kind/:id/log` SSE. Requests accept only local same
-origin browser traffic or local SDK calls. The public extension catalog excludes commands and envir
onment variables; configuration-editing endpoints are for trusted local calls only. See HOST.md for
the complete routes.
Extensions use a `butler.json` in each directory; see the schema for all fields. The SDK runner send
s events using `BUTLER_HOST_URL`; `BUTLER_GUARDIAN_URL` is only a compatibility alias for old extens
ions, not a new configuration entry point.
**Delegations:** tools/services may declare steps requiring judgment in their manifests. The Host de
legates them to a new Butler Session (`POST /delegations`, blocking until submission, timeout, or fa
ilure). Only the Host drives sessions: it creates a butler-preset session with `sessionController.cr
eate`, delivers a `prompt` using the delegation ID as requestId, and calls `cancel` on timeout. The
session may use only the declared tools and `butler_delegation_submit`; results are validated agains
t the declared schema. Results with `risk: confirm` remain pending in the observation area. `POST /r
uns/:runId/steps/:i/confirm` uses the same owner-only gate as card review (`X-Butler-Review` plus sa
me-origin Origin or authenticated desktop forwarding). If DSH does not provide `sessionController.pr
ompt`, `/delegations` returns 503 and callers use their own fallback. See the SDK README for usage.
## Unified MCP service (Butler Framework MCP standard)
Three layers communicate only through manifests and the MCP protocol:
| Layer | Responsibility | Exclusions |
| Framework (`spec/butler.schema.json`) | Defines the `mcp` registration block: `transport: "stdio"`
, `command`, optional `cwd/env/namespace/timeoutSec`; tools/services only | No independently exposed

`http`/`url` forms |
| Host (`src/host/mcp-hub.ts`) | Derives providers from scan results without a
second registry; starts stdio subprocesses through `Spawner` on demand; aggregates as `<namespace>_
_<tool>`; serves stateless Streamable HTTP at `/myspace-butler/api/mcp`; adds/removes providers on r
escan and restarts them when idle; terminates with the managed range on App exit | Does not import e

xtension code or interpret business parameters |
| Extension | Implements a stdio MCP server | Does
not listen on an MCP port or call Host internals; may reject direct client connections using `BUTLER
_MCP_CHANNEL=butler-hub` |
Clients configure just one address: `http://127.0.0.1:19387/myspace-butler/api/mcp` (the desktop pro
file's App port). `GET /api/mcp/status` reports provider status, exposed tool names, namespace confl
icts, and rejected tool names. The default namespace replaces `-` in the ID with `_`; exposed names
must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`. Nonmatching tools are not exposed and appear in status. A provid
er crash affects only that provider: calls return an `isError` result and startup is retried after 5
seconds, without affecting other providers. The security boundary matches other Host APIs: loopback
only, rejecting cross-site Origins (the DNS rebinding protection required by MCP).

## Dashboard display preferences
Services and tools each retain a “Show all / Show resident” mode. The heading arrow switches the dis
play scope rather than collapsing the whole section. “Display management · N stored” is a single ent
ry opening a drawer with all items. There you can mark items resident, operate them directly, and sa
ve or cancel display changes; card menus can also store individual items or mark them resident.
Storing an item is exclusively a manual choice, not inferred from autoStart, running state, or usage
frequency; it does not change manifests or start/stop processes. Newly registered items are residen
t by default. Search always covers names, IDs, and descriptions of all items, marking matching store
d items. Clearing search restores the previous mode. Sorting is disabled when some items are hidden
or a search is active; showing all enables sorting.
Preferences use the Host's existing `layout.json` (version 1, adding optional `display.services/tool
s: { mode: 'all' | 'resident', stored: string[] }`), remaining compatible with old files. The page a
nd sidebar share them, and they survive refreshes. “Reset order” clears only `order`, not display pr
eferences. A failed save rolls back the display while retaining the drawer draft; older polling resu
lts do not overwrite newly saved settings.
